item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-21
item.description:
# Episode Summary
This Saturday episode tracks three major developments shaping markets and politics: the escalating Iran conflict's devastating impact on global energy supplies, with strikes across nine countries disrupting the Strait of Hormuz and forcing the U.S. to lift Iranian oil sanctions in hopes of relieving pressure at the pump; a federal court's ruling striking down Pentagon press restrictions as unconstitutional, protecting journalists' access during wartime; and insights from the latest Dividend Cafe cautioning investors against building portfolios on military speculation while offering a reality check on private credit contagion fears. Throughout, energy prices emerge as both an economic pressure point and a political wildcard heading into the midterms.

# Dad's Daily Digest: March 20th
This episode examines three critical stories shaping markets and geopolitics: the widening gap between U.S. and Israeli strategic goals in the Iran conflict, which threatens to eliminate diplomatic off-ramps; a record 7.7 million student loan defaults totaling $181 billion, signaling underappreciated consumer stress beyond headline inflation figures; and the evolving AI investment landscape, where defense and national security applications are reshaping the thesis that volatility exposed back in January. Together, these threads reveal growing tensions between geopolitical stability, household financial resilience, and shifting patterns in how capital is being deployed.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-19
item.description:
# Middle East Escalation and the Fed's Impossible Dilemma
This morning brings two major developments: Israel struck Iran's South Pars gas field, one of the world's largest natural gas reserves, escalating the Middle East conflict and threatening global LNG supplies through neighboring Qatar—a move that has oil prices surging and markets bracing for potential energy shocks across Europe and Asia. Simultaneously, the Fed faces a deepening bind as supply-side inflation pressures collide with recession concerns, leaving monetary policy tools that can't solve energy-driven price shocks, while Jerome Powell signals he's staying put amid tension with the White House over rate cut demands.
